- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.3), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model often overcorrects in next 3–5 days; reduce forecast by 1–3% in following periods.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 5-day average, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction, especially if sentiment shifts sharply mid-horizon.
- When sentiment is high and price is falling, model often fails to recognize downward momentum; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day for 3–5 days after sentiment peak.
